question: If the pH value of river water is _________, then its water is considered to be polluted by acidic waste.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Less than 7**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If the **pH value of river water is less than 7**, it indicates that the water is acidic, which means it has been polluted by acidic waste.
 
• **pH scale**:
 
• The pH scale measures how acidic or alkaline a substance is. It ranges from 0 to 14.
 
• A pH value of **7** is neutral, meaning it is neither acidic nor alkaline.
 
• A pH **less than 7** indicates that the water is acidic.
 
• A pH **greater than 7** indicates that the water is alkaline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When the **pH value of water drops below 7 (becomes acidic), it can be caused by the presence of acidic pollutants, such as industrial waste, acid rain, or untreated sewage.** This can harm aquatic life, disturb ecosystems, and affect the quality of the water for human consumption and other uses.
